Definition: to be startled (by a sudden alarm); hence, to fear in general
BiblicalUsage: Pâchad is to tremble, to fear, to stand in awe. The disobedient live in dread day and night, the prophet says I will trust and not be afraid, the psalmist asks whom shall I fear when the LORD is his light, and the happy man fears always while the hard-hearted fall into mischief.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that fear is not the enemy of faith but its beginning. The man who fears the LORD rightly has nothing left to be afraid of.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
